business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BITs with over 80 countries including the United States (1995), United Kingdom (2014), Germany (2008), France, Brazil, Mexico

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and Spanish domestic sanctions screening using compliant tools per Law 10/2010 and AML standards

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish using the Latin alphabet; foreign-language names require official translation and approval
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words indicating banking, savings, insurance or investment services without prior authorization
Names confusing with public administration or protected entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Ministry of Justice or competent registry body within one month of rejection notice; subsequent judicial review available if administrative remedies exhausted

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are fully permissible and widely accepted for SL companies provided the address is verifiable and meets notary/registry requirements
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk of unannounced physical inspections for standard SL formations; reliance on documentation and self-certification unless red flags trigger review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July 2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20-24 (incorporation), Article 33 (registration), Article 134 (governing body); complemented by Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Regulation of the Commercial Registry (Royal Decree 1784/1996)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification; Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (Provincial Commercial Registry) for incorporation inscription
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) presented for registration in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum registered capital of EUR 1.00 (post-Law 18/2022); capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; cash contributions require a bank certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) issued by a Spanish credit institution, or an auditor's waiver report for non-cash contributions; no escrow account is mandatory beyond the deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: (1) the founding shareholders approve the public deed of incorporation of Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada and irrevocably subscribe and fully pay in 3,850 participations comprising the EUR 3,850.00 registered capital, receipt acknowledged; (2) the registered office is adopted at Calle Gran Vía 28, 28013 Madrid, Spain, and the company shall be registered in the Registro Mercantil de Madrid; (3) Ana García is appointed Sole Administrator, Javier López Alternate Administrator, and Carmen Ruiz Secretary, each accepting office; (4) the Sole Administrator is authorized to complete tax, social security, and municipal licensing registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the Company Name (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) via the CIRCE electronic portal or paper application at the Madrid office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form (hoja electrónica) requesting a negative name certificate, listing up to three alternative corporate names; the registry verifies absence of identical or phonetically confusing names; certificate is valid for three months and must accompany the deed.
required_dossiers: Completed name certification application form (Modelo de solicitud de certificación)
NIE or DNI of the incorporator or legal representative
List of up to three proposed company names in order of preference
Proof of payment of the Central Registry fee (tasa / arancel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certification is denied for resemblance to an existing name, re-file with alternative names; if the registry erroneously rejects, lodge an administrative appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Provisional Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank, savings bank, or cooperative credit union) lawfully operating in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account in the name 'SL en constitución'; deposit the fully subscribed capital in cash; obtain the bank's certificate of deposit, stating the depositor, amount and account number, or instruct the notary to waive the certificate if non-cash contributions are covered by an auditor's report.
required_dossiers: Name certificate (certificación negativa)
Draft articles of association (borrador de estatutos)
Passport or NIE of each founding shareholder
AML/KYC documentation per Law 10/2010, including source-of-funds declaration
Corporate account instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account for AML deficiencies, supplement the source-of-funds evidence and reapply; alternatively, execute the deed with a notarial deposit or auditor's non-cash contribution waiver, removing the bank certificate requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Spanish civil law notary) within the notarial district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and final bylaws to the notary; all founders (or granted attorneys) appear personally and sign the deed; the notary verifies legal capacity and capital legality; the notary then sends the deed electronically to AEAT within 10 business days for provisional NIF issuance.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación social (valid at execution date)
Bank certificate of capital deposit, or auditor's waiver for non-cash contributions
Estatutos sociales (bylaws) in final form, duplicated
DNI/NIE and passports of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects an expired name certificate or incomplete capital proof, cure by obtaining fresh documents and rescheduling; if the deed text contains drafting errors, execute an amendment before the same notary before registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Request for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Provincial Office of Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 business days following notarization, file Modelo 036 (declaración censal de alta) attaching a certified copy of the deed; the company is assigned a provisional CIF/NIF immediately; the filing also registers the company in the Census of Obligated Entities.
required_dossiers: First copy (primera copia) of the public deed
Completed Modelo 036 form with economic activity codes (CNAE 6430)
Original deed copy sufficient for the tax office
NIE/DNI of the Sole Administrator
Proof of official domicile in Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provisional NIF is not issued due to missing data, complete Modelo 036 rectificativo and resubmit; if the deed copy lacks the notary's electronic transmission number, present the registry presentation receipt and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil de Madrid (provincial Commercial Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first authorized copy of the deed and the provisional NIF at the Registry office; the registrar verifies legality of the deed, capital, and bylaws; positive inscription confers legal personality; registration must be completed within one month of deed execution.
required_dossiers: Primera copia autorizada de la escritura pública de constitución
Provisional NIF certificate
Proof of Modelo 036 filing (AEAT receipt)
Paid registry fee receipt (arancel del Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'calificación negativa' listing defects (e.g., unlawful bylaws clause, incorrect capital allocation), remedy the defects within the stated period and re-present; if the calificación is unjustified, appeal before the Juzgado de lo Mercantil.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Definitive NIF, Social Security Registration, and Labor Workplace Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); labor authority of Madrid (Comunidad de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once inscription is recorded, return to AEAT with the registry certificate to obtain the definitive NIF automatically; register the company and the administrator with TGSS using Modelo TA.1 and the Employer Registration Form F.011; notify the occupation of the workplace ('comunicación de apertura del centro de trabajo') within 30 days of start of activity.
required_dossiers: Certificación del Registro Mercantil acreditativo de la inscripción
Registered public deed
Definitive Modelo 036 update
Modelo TA.1 and F.011 forms
Occupational risk assessment (evaluación de riesgos laborales) and workplace plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT fails to validate the definitive NIF, present the registry certification directly and request the upgrade; for TGSS mismatches, file a rectificación request with the deed and NIF; if the labor authority identifies defects, correct the technical assessment and resubmit within the given term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Opening License and Physical Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Gerencia de Urbanismo, Permisos y Licencias; authorized inspection body (OCA) for fire safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'licencia de apertura' application including a descriptive project, fire safety technical certificate issued by an authorized OCA, occupational risk assessment, environmental filing where applicable, and proof of legal use of premises; the license is granted by silence after the legal period if no objection is raised.
required_dossiers: Memoria descriptiva de actividad (descriptive technical report under CNAE 6430)
Fire safety certificate (certificado de extinción y protección contra incendios) from an OCA
Occupational health and safety plan per Law 31/1995 and RD 486/1997
Proof of title or lease of the premises (escritura or contrato de arrendamiento)
Municipal fee payment (tasa por licencia de apertura)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies the license or imposes conditions, supplement the technical dossier and file a written appeal to the Alcaldía within one month; if the denial is administrative silence, request an express resolution and thereafter pursue judicial review before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria y de la Pequeña y Mediana Empresa (Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism), acting jointly with the Ayuntamiento de Madrid for non-industrial classified activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Municipal de Apertura y Funcionamiento (Local Opening and Operation Permit for administrative office premises)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) — Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from Full EIA: the activity (administration of employee share incentive plans) is not listed in the annexes of Law 21/2013; only an Environmental Activity Registration (Registro de Actividades Potencialmente Contaminantes, RAPC) is required for the office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge: domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewer ordinances and RD 1021/2007; VOC and solvent emission limits of RD 100/2011 are not applicable to office activity; general waste must be managed under Law 7/2022 (circular economy), and electronic waste under RD 110/2015 requiring registered authorized waste handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificado de protección contra incendios) issued by an authorized inspection body (OCA) verifying occupancy load, extinguishers, and emergency exits; structural load assessment of the leased premises; workplace clearance under RD 486/1997 (workplaces), RD 487/1997 (manual handling), and prior occupational health and safety evaluation registered with the labor authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency, accessible via the official portal at www.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish resident entities including Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtain NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) upon incorporation through the Registro Mercantil Central. Foreign entities must register with the AEAT to secure a NIE or NIF, followed by tax registration via the Sede Electrónica or eAdmin portals, submitting incorporation documents, articles of association, proof of address, and economic activity details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide check-the-box elections. Available mechanisms include election of the General Regime for SMEs (PYME), specific holding company regimes, and fiduciary tax treatments for employee share ownership trusts under Royal Decree 1288/2018, which may permit tax deferrals on equity transfers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido - IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 30,000 EUR annual taxable turnover threshold triggering mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers must issue electronic invoices exclusively through the ENI (Electronic Invoice) system. Real-time fiscal clearance requires transmission to the AEAT within four business days with mandatory digital stamping and API integration for enterprises above specified volume thresholds.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported outside the EU upon verified export documentation. Offshore services to non-resident clients qualify for zero-rating under reverse charge or specific export service provisions, requiring proof of service performance and customer non-residency in Spain.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims incur penalties of 100% to 200% of evaded tax plus interest and surcharges. Retrospective clawback of VAT credits or refunds occurs upon audit for insufficient documentation, subject to a four-year limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-investment and certain statistical reporting functions also involve the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and applies EU Treaty free-movement-of-capital rules. Current-account payments, trade settlements, service fees, payroll, dividends, interest and ordinary repatriation are generally freely transferable without exchange controls or mandatory conversion into euros. Capital-account transactions are also generally liberalised, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, prudential rules, foreign-investment screening, statistical declarations and bank due diligence. A Spanish SL may generally remit dividends, interest, royalties, liquidation proceeds and other permitted payments to non-residents after corporate approvals, accounting support and tax compliance. The principal remittance hurdles are distributable-profit and net-asset tests, withholding tax, applicable treaty or EU exemption conditions, beneficial-owner verification, transfer-pricing support, thin-capitalisation or interest-limitation rules, sanctions screening, and documentation of shareholder or lender status. Dividend distributions normally require a 19% Spanish withholding-tax analysis, subject to applicable treaty relief and potential EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption where all statutory ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction before executing high-value or unusual cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may normally remain in euros or foreign currency in accounts maintained with Spanish or other EEA financial institutions, subject to the bank's account terms and reporting obligations. There is generally no statutory deadline requiring an exporter to repatriate or convert export proceeds. Banks and payment service providers may collect transaction information for payment statistics, tax records, trade reporting, sanctions compliance and anti-money-laundering controls. Customs, VAT, Intrastat and statistical reporting deadlines remain applicable independently of receipt collection. Physical cash or bearer instruments of EUR 10,000 or more entering or leaving the EU require the applicable customs declaration; movements of cash or equivalent instruments within Spain at or above EUR 100,000 generally require the applicable prior declaration. These cash thresholds do not apply to ordinary bank-to-bank transfers.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine SEPA collections, payroll-related payments and supplier transfers, provided the provider is an authorised bank or electronic-money institution established in the EEA and lawfully passported into Spain. An EMI safeguards customer funds but does not provide a bank deposit or ordinary deposit-guarantee protection. An offshore provider outside the EEA cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services into Spain merely through a website. The Spanish SL must verify the provider's authorisation, passporting status, safeguarding model, IBAN jurisdiction, payment-fund segregation, transaction limits, sanctions controls, data-processing terms and account-closure procedures. Fintech accounts should not be the sole treasury account for tax, payroll, fiduciary, capital or high-value cross-border flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not generally require every director to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents and beneficial-owner verification. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, original or notarised documents, a Spanish-resident signatory, a local representative, or a live compliance interview based on risk, ownership complexity, foreign shareholders, trust-like arrangements, high-risk countries, unusual payment flows or inability to verify identity remotely. Directors, authorised signatories and ultimate beneficial owners should be prepared to complete individual KYC and source-of-funds interviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, layered foreign holding companies or an employee stock ownership structure that resembles a trust or fiduciary arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry extracts for every ownership layer; constitutional documents; ownership chart to natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; director and signatory resolutions; employee-plan rules; trustee, administrator or fiduciary appointment documents; beneficiary classes; voting and economic-rights analysis; written explanation that the entity is not being used to conceal ownership; and independent legal or accounting memorandum where Spanish trust-law characterization is relevant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated business is described as an ESOP trust although Spain does not have a general domestic trust-equivalent vehicle, creating uncertainty over legal ownership of shares and funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish-law corporate and securities-law analysis; plan constitution; employer, participant and administrator agreements; share custody arrangements; broker or custodian agreement; segregation and reconciliation policy; beneficial-owner and control-rights matrix; tax treatment memorandum; and confirmation that the SL is not conducting regulated collective investment, payment, custody, investment-services or fiduciary activity without authorisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity is inconsistent with the declared low-risk profile, including rapid movement of large third-party funds, pass-through payments, high cash turnover or unexplained payments to employees and shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume and counterparty schedule; payroll and employee-plan payment files; approved payment matrix; invoices and contracts; bank statements; accounting ledgers; reconciliation procedures; source-and-use-of-funds schedule; and explanation of expected peak balances and payment cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital originates from a foreign shareholder, employee investment vehicle, private fund, trust, nominee or unrelated third party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; corporate approvals; proof of ownership; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; originating bank statements; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funder; beneficial-owner certification; foreign-investment filing evidence where applicable; payment instruction identifying the exact legal purpose; and confirmation that no third-party settlement is being used without a documented legal basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Country, counterparty, bank or payment purpose generates sanctions, proliferation-financing, corruption or enhanced-due-diligence concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full counterparty KYC; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user statement; shipping and customs documents where relevant; commercial contract; invoice; beneficial-owner declaration; adverse-media review; tax-residency certificates; independent compliance sign-off; and documented escalation and approval records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors or shareholders cannot provide acceptable tax-residency, address, identification or corporate-authority evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or otherwise bank-acceptable registry extracts; certified translations; valid passports or national identity documents; recent utility bills or government address evidence; tax-residency certificates; notarised powers of attorney; incumbency certificates; board minutes; and a Spanish contact address or authorised representative where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value dividend, interest, royalty, liquidation or shareholder-loan payments lack tax and accounting support.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved financial statements; distributable-profit calculation; shareholder resolution; loan agreement and arm's-length interest analysis; withholding-tax computation; treaty-residence and beneficial-ownership certificates; EU exemption documentation where applicable; transfer-pricing file; payment schedule; and evidence of tax filing or payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a non-Spanish IBAN, virtual IBAN or fintech account causes the bank to question account ownership, safeguarding or operational control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licence and passporting evidence; account-holder certificate; safeguarding confirmation; terms of business; bank or EMI account statement; reconciliation policy; authorised-user list; transaction-limit schedule; and written explanation of the relationship between the Spanish SL, the IBAN provider and each payment counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a bank account held in the exact legal name of the Spanish SL. Route share capital, share premium and shareholder loans directly from the subscribing shareholder or documented lender through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT customer credit transfer for non-SEPA payments. Identify the payment purpose as share capital, share premium, shareholder loan or other precisely documented funding; avoid generic third-party funding descriptions. Maintain the subscription or loan agreement, board and shareholder approvals, bank-origin evidence, source-of-funds file, beneficial-owner documents, accounting entry and reconciliation to the incoming amount. For incorporation, the bank may issue a capital-deposit certificate or equivalent evidence; a Spanish SL can generally be incorporated with nominal capital of EUR 1 under the current Spanish Companies Act framework, subject to the statutory special rules applicable to capital below EUR 3,000, so a capital escrow account is not invariably required. Foreign investment and statistical declarations must be assessed under the applicable Spanish Ministry of Economy regime, including any special-sector screening or suspension rules. Do not split payments to avoid bank monitoring or reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's current ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments, with complete originator, beneficiary, purpose, invoice and intermediary-bank data. Use documentary Commercial Letters of Credit under applicable UCP 600 rules for higher-risk goods, new counterparties or jurisdictional risk; use standby letters of credit and demand guarantees where commercially appropriate and supported by bank credit approval. Retain purchase orders, invoices, contracts, customs records, transport documents, import or export evidence, VAT records, sanctions checks and three-way payment matching. Spain does not impose a universal statutory payment-purpose-code system equivalent to certain controlled-currency jurisdictions, but banks may require internal purpose classifications and transaction narratives. Trade, VAT, customs, Intrastat, statistical and tax reporting remains separate from the payment rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorised bank or investment firm for documented commercial exposures, subject to MiFID II classification, appropriateness or suitability requirements where applicable, confirmation, valuation, collateral and internal-limit controls.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to counterparty authorisation, local-market legality, sanctions screening, EMIR reporting and documented underlying exposure. NDFs are generally unnecessary for ordinary EUR-denominated Spanish operations unless the exposure is in a non-convertible or restricted currency.
Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, EMIR obligations, collateral and valuation controls.

FX options and option collars for documented commercial exposures, where permitted by the authorised counterparty and approved under the company's derivatives policy; speculative trading should be prohibited unless separately authorised and legally permissible.

Treasury controls should include board-approved risk limits, hedge-designation records where hedge accounting is used, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, confirmation matching, daily exposure reporting, counterparty limits, collateral procedures, independent valuation and accounting under applicable Spanish GAAP or IFRS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Deposit of Annual Accounts: balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, notes and, where applicable, audit report and directors' report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office; filing data transmitted to the Registro Mercantil Central and published as a deposit notice in the BORME.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within six months after the financial year end (by 30 June for calendar-year accounts); the deposit must be completed within one month after approval (by 31 July for calendar-year accounts).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 1,200 - 6,000 on the company and its directors for omission; continuing default blocks all further company inscriptions (cierre registral), including share transfers, appointments and certificates. Non-deposit for two consecutive years escalates to loss of registry standing and may trigger dissolution/liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalización de Libros Obligatorios (Annual legalization and closing of statutory accounting and corporate books: journal, inventory/annual accounts and corporate minute books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (electronic legalización telemática service of the Commercial Registry).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounting books must be closed and legalized within the first four months after the financial year end (by 30 April for calendar-year accounts); the Libro Registro de Socios must remain permanently available and be legalized as required by the Registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Un-legalized books lose evidentiary value in commercial and tax disputes; the Commercial Registry may refuse subsequent filings; tax inspection may impose penalties for accounting irregularities under Article 200 of the Ley General Tributaria, with fines up to EUR 6,000 plus the value of irregular records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real (Annual beneficial ownership confirmation for the SL, including ESOP-trust ultimate employee beneficiaries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central - Registro de Titularidad Real (UBO registry module) and AEAT via the UBO schedule within Form 200.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation accompanies the deposit of annual accounts (by 31 July for calendar-year accounts); any transfer of participations or change in ultimate ownership, including ESOP allocations and vesting transfers, must be recorded without delay and reflected on the next annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML fines under Law 10/2010: minor offences up to EUR 60,000; serious offences up to EUR 150,000; very serious offences up to EUR 1,000,000 or 5% of own funds if higher; the Commercial Registry's closure of the company's folio also applies where the UBO declaration is omitted with the accounts deposit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Form 200 annual corporate income tax return, incorporating final financial data and UBO disclosures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 25 calendar days after the end of the six-month post-year-end period: 1 - 25 July for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneous filing surcharge of 1% per month on tax due (maximum 20%) plus late-payment interest and penalty interest; unpaid corporate tax may trigger enforcement against the SL's assets and administrator/director liability. Form 200 default alone does not cause strike-off but reinforces registry closure and enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies when the SL meets at least two of the following conditions for two consecutive financial years under Article 263 of RDL 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital): balance-sheet total exceeds EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for listed, supervised financial, insurance or group-consolidated entities; a voluntary audit may be required by shareholders holding at least 5% of the capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP under the Código de Comercio and Plan General de Contabilidad (RD 1514/2007); SMEs may apply the PGC de PYMES (RD 1515/2007) subject to size thresholds; annual accounts are filed in XBRL format. IFRS-EU is reserved for consolidated accounts of listed groups and is not the primary GAAP for a non-listed SL. Commercial Code Article 30 imposes six-year statutory retention of accounting books, while the Ley General Tributaria extends retention of tax-support documentation to ten years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an updated register of ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons ultimately holding or controlling more than 25% of participations or voting rights, including employees or beneficiaries holding through the ESOP trust). Any transfer of participations upon option exercise, vesting or trust allocation must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios before votes or dividends are recognized; the annual UBO declaration is submitted with the deposit of annual accounts, updated in the Registro Mercantil Central UBO module and included in Form 200. Non-resident or trust-held participations must be mapped to the underlying natural-person beneficiaries on each annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members/Shareholders of the SL, reflecting every ESOP-trust share transfer and beneficiary allocation)
Libro de Actas (Minute Book of shareholders' general meetings and director/administrator meetings)
Libros de Contabilidad (legalized accounting books: Diario, Inventario y Cuentas Anuales, including the closing annual statement)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 1,500 per year (Spanish virtual/registered office and compliance secretarial package for a non-licensed SL)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 9,000 per annual certified audit (statutory or voluntarily agreed); preparation-only chartered accountancy is typically USD 1,200 - 4,000; complex ESOP-trust accounting increases the fee.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard CIT (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); 15% reduced rate for newly created qualifying S.L.s in the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (Art. 29.1 LIS), subject to the anti-abuse exclusion for entities whose main activity is managing a securities portfolio; 30% for credit institutions and hydrocarbon entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% new-entity rate (Art. 29.1 LIS, generally unavailable to ESOP asset-holding vehicles); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS) where a 5% or more holding is maintained for one year and the subsidiary is subject to a comparable 10%+ foreign tax; ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) regime for qualifying holding entities; R&D and job-creation tax credits; reinvestment relief for extraordinary income; no wealth taxes at entity level. Loss relief: net operating losses are carried forward indefinitely (no statutory expiry) for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2015, subject to annual offset caps of 70% of taxable base for entities with net turnover between EUR 20M and EUR 60M, 50% for EUR 60M-EUR 100M, and 25% above EUR 100M, with a minimum annual offset of EUR 1M always available.
